newsitem.title: USA: CRP bill adds confusion to farming - USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: CRP bill adds confusion to farming - USDA's Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan said Tuesday he very strongly opposed a bill expected to be debated later in the day in the U.S. House to allow a one-year extension of Conservation Reserve contracts.

The bill, sponsored by House Agriculture chairman Bob Smith, "would keep millions of acres in retirement...at a time when U.S. and foreign wheat stocks are unusually low," Glickman wrote in a letter to Smith.
Rather than helping farmers with fall-planted crops, Glickman said the bill would only add confusion to this year's massive turnover of contracts covering 21 million acres.
It also would hobble USDA's efforts to heighten the environmental benefits from land in the long-term reserve, he wrote, by keeping less fragile land under contract.
Smith has said the bill was needed because USDA might not give farmers with fall-planted crops adequate notice if their bids to enroll land in the reserve had been accepted.
USDA was on track to notify farmers by late May if bids were accepted or rejected, Glickman said.

Farmers have several options if they want to get CRP land ready for crops, the letter said. They include an "early-out" exit and the usual provisions for fieldwork in the final year of a contract. If farmers destroy field cover and later learn their bids were accepted, USDA will cover part of the cost of reseeding, Glickman wrote.
In areas where fall planting normally occurs in September, "USDA has in the past and will again allow some planting to begin without contract payment reductions," he wrote.
